historicalSituation:
During the Seven Days Battles, George B. McClellan withdrew the Army of the Potomac toward the James River. Its route passed through the narrow Glendale crossroads before reaching Malvern Hill. Robert E. Lee attempted to converge several Confederate columns on Glendale and cut the Union army in two. Jackson stalled at White Oak Swamp, Huger was delayed, Holmes made little progress, and Magruder failed to participate effectively. Only the forces of James Longstreet and A. P. Hill mounted a major attack from the west along the Long Bridge Road axis.

Their immediate opponent was Brig. Gen. George A. McCall’s Pennsylvania Reserve division, deployed across the open Whitlock and Sykes farm fields with artillery forward and infantry behind. Repeated Confederate assaults captured and recaptured Federal batteries and drove parts of McCall’s division from the fields. Late in the day A. P. Hill’s troops penetrated the wooded ground between the Whitlock and Nelson farms, threatening Willis Church Road. Reinforcements from Sedgwick’s division counterattacked and preserved the Union retreat route. The Confederates held much of the original battlefield and captured guns, but failed in their larger objective of cutting off McClellan’s army.
deploymentNotes:
Union deploys first.

Meade: north of Long Bridge Road in the Sykes field sector.
Seymour: south of Long Bridge Road toward Whitlock.
Simmons: behind McCall as the divisional reserve.
Randol: north of Long Bridge Road.
Cooper and Kerns: south of the road.
Diederichs and Knieriem: toward the Whitlock end of the line.
Robinson: northern woods/right flank.
Burns: Nelson field / Willis Church Road.
Dana and Sully: off-table reinforcements.

Confederates enter from the west.

First wave: Kemper, Jenkins, Pickett.
Second wave: Wilcox, Pryor, Featherston.
A. P. Hill’s brigades form the final major assault wave.
victoryText:
The scenario is about breaking or preserving the Union retreat route, not simply inflicting casualties.

Confederate Major Victory: Break through the Union rear position and establish uncontested infantry on or beyond the Willis Church Road objective line.

Confederate Minor Victory: Control the Whitlock/Sykes fields and penetrate the central woods/Nelson approaches, but fail to cut Willis Church Road.

Union Major Victory: Hold or recapture the principal Whitlock/Sykes position while keeping Willis Church Road secure.

Union Minor Victory: Lose the forward Whitlock/Sykes fields but maintain a formed defensive line protecting Willis Church Road through the end of the game.

Historical result: Confederate tactical gain / Union operational success.

Design Notes for Studio

Use the current square Glendale schematic as the authoritative 24"×24" battlefield crop. Preserve the field/wood geometry and main ravine from the NPS 1860 reconstruction. Do not treat every visible drainage, crop field, fence, or building as functional terrain.

For ACW force generation, do not automatically compress a brigade to 2–3 Battle Axe units. Where the historical regiment is identified, generate one Infantry unit per regiment as the first test assumption. If the resulting board proves too congested, address that during playtesting rather than silently reducing the historical OOB. The current ACW Studio doctrine is explicitly brigade-centric while maneuvering individual regiments.

McCall: 1 or 2
Meade: 2

Robinson: 2
Sedgwick: 2
Burns: 1 or 2

Confederate

Longstreet: 2 or 3
A. P. Hill: 2
Kemper: 2
Wilcox: 2
Field: 2
other brigade commanders mostly 1–2

observations.value:

Reinforcements from Sedgwick’s division counterattacked and preserved the Union retreat route. The Confederates held much of the original battlefield and captured guns, but failed in their larger objective of cutting off McClellan’s army.

The battlefield is a rural agricultural landscape of large cultivated clearings separated by substantial woodland and wooded drainage corridors. McCall described his immediate front as roughly 800 yards wide and at least 1,000 yards deep. The principal battle ground was formed by the adjoining Whitlock and Richard and Isaac Sykes farms. The NPS reconstruction identifies these open fields as the core battlefield.

Key features for the scenario:

Long Bridge Road: principal Confederate attack axis through the center.
Whitlock Farm and field: major fighting on the Union left; site of batteries and improvised rail breastworks.
Richard and Isaac Sykes fields: major fighting north of Long Bridge Road.
Central wooded ravine / Western Run drainage: meaningful difficult/broken terrain separating portions of the battlefield.
Nelson field: final Federal defensive ground west of Willis Church Road.
Willis Church Road: operational objective and Union line of retreat.
Major woods: normal Woods terrain.
Cultivated fields/crops: Open terrain; visual only.
Minor streams/drainage: decorative only.
Most fences: decorative; only specifically designated historical sections should affect play.
Whitlock breastworks: short Defensive feature representing the improvised rail works built by elements of the 12th Pennsylvania Reserves.
